gaps: No existing CLI or SDK exposes Naver's transparency-report statistics; the series is embedded in the Privacy Center's CMS page payload and otherwise only visible in the browser
The statistics arrive as one raw JSON blob per page — there is no per-category or per-period query surface
patterns: Transparency dashboards elsewhere (Google, Kakao) expose one period at a time; Naver ships the entire series in a single CMS payload, which favors local tidying over repeated calls

novel_features.name: Tidy statistics series
novel_features.description: The full 2012-present transparency series as one tidy table — one row per half-year and request category with request/processed/provided/average counts and compliance rates.
novel_features.rationale: The raw endpoint returns 28 wide entries with 24 cryptic per-category columns each; the CLI reshapes them into the long-form rows analysis tools expect and decodes the category prefixes into readable names.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for any question about Naver's government data-request trends — it replaces hand-parsing specificAreaJson.

novel_features.name: Whitepaper library index
novel_features.description: List the NAVER Privacy Report and privacy-whitepaper publications (titles, authors, attached documents) from the report library.
novel_features.rationale: The publication list lives inside the NAVER_REPORT page's specificAreaJson; the CLI surfaces it as a flat list agents can search and cite.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to find Naver's own published analyses and the downloadable report documents behind the statistics.

novel_features.name: Half-year narrative summaries
novel_features.description: Naver's own per-half-year commentary on the statistics, HTML-stripped to plain text.
novel_features.rationale: Each statistics entry carries a guideEditorHtml narrative that explains anomalies (mergers, warrant spikes); the CLI extracts it as readable text next to the period it explains.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before interpreting a spike or drop in the numbers — Naver usually explains it in the period's own commentary.

narrative.headline: Naver's transparency-report series — Korea's first, published since 2015 — as tidy per-category statistics instead of a CMS page blob.
narrative.value_prop: The Naver Privacy Center ships its entire 2012-present government data-request series (warrants, communication data, restriction measures, log records) inside one CMS page payload. This CLI unpacks it: `statistics` emits tidy per-period, per-category rows, `summaries` extracts Naver's own commentary, and `whitepapers` indexes the downloadable NAVER Privacy Report library.

quickstart.comment: Verify connectivity — the API is public, no credentials needed
The full transparency series as tidy CSV rows
The raw CMS payload if you need every field

troubleshoots.fix: The page code is unknown to the CMS — codes are case-sensitive strings like TRANSPARENCY_REPORT_STATISTICS or NAVER_REPORT; check the code against the Privacy Center site.
'-' marks categories Naver no longer complies with (no communication user information provided since October 2012); treat it as not-applicable, not zero.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for questions about South Korean government requests for Naver user data — warrant volumes, compliance rates, log-record requests — and for Naver's own privacy publications. It is the only machine-friendly path to the full statistics series.
anti_triggers: Do not use it for Naver's developer APIs (search, maps, Papago, CLOVA) — this wraps only the Privacy Center content API
Do not use it for content-moderation or copyright-takedown statistics; Naver's transparency report covers government data requests only
Content is Korean-only — do not expect localized English field values
